question.problem: The velocity $v,$ in meters per second, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨-{t}^{2},\,1,\,t⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1\,\text{s}.$
question.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}.
$$

First, we evaluate $v(1):$

$$
v(1)=⟨-1,\,1,\,1⟩
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and evaluating it at $t=1,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2t,\,0,\,1⟩, \\ a(1) & =⟨-2,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(1)\times a(1),||v(1)||,$ and $||v(1)\times a(1)||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1)\times a(1) & =⟨-1,\,1,\,1⟩\times ⟨-2,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨1,-1,2⟩, \\ ||v(1)|| & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3}, \\ ||v(1)\times a(1)|| & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration at $t=1,$ and we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v(1)\times a(1)||}{||v(1)||} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the normal component of acceleration is $\sqrt{2}\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$
